message.content: The evidence is decisive: c1 and c3 are confirmed in-scope runtime failures (run(x) ≠ reference(x) at both N=64 and N=128, exact-equality contract violated), c2 rebutted, Skeptic signed off with no new claims. Recording the verdict.

function.arguments: {"confidence": 0.99, "decisive_claims": ["c1", "c3"], "reason": "The contract (problem.txt) requires run(x) to exactly equal the cyclic modular DFT (tolerance 0/0, canonical [0,3328] representatives, natural-order output) for every canonical int32 input at N∈{64,128} on CUDA — the exact domain the probes exercised. Confirmed claim c1: on CUDA, run(x) != reference(x) at both widths — single-coefficient unit rows mismatch thousands of positions (N=64: 2368, N=128: 9472), random rows mismatch (1023 / 2047), extreme all-3328 rows and even constant rows mismatch nearly every position. Confirmed claim c3: at N=128 the kernel output equals the bit-reversal permutation of the reference (bitrev_perm_match=true), i.e. non-natural-order output, a direct violation of the \"output position k is frequency k in natural order\" clause; constant rows additionally fail (127/128), showing a further arithmetic/wrap defect. The Montgomery reduction (c2) was exhaustively rebutted, which does not mitigate the confirmed output failures. All inputs tested are squarely inside the stated public domain (int32, [B,N] with B≤128, canonical values, contiguous CUDA). No open claims remain and the Skeptic recorded no further concerns after reviewing all evidence.", "verdict": "reject"}
